summary: Benton County, OR lookout (Oregon Dept. of Forestry) built 1934-35, staffed 1935-42, removed 1968; concrete footings remain per a trip report.

facts.design: 40' wooden tower with 14'x14' cab (1935); 40' treated timber L-4 tower reported for 1951
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1968 (1969 in one source); concrete footings remain near the summit per a trip report

events.note: Eugene paper, Oct 1934: tower and house practically completed. FFLOS and Wikipedia date it 1935.
Mrs. Norman Sapp and infant son at the station with Mr. Sapp (July 1935); earliest staffing item found
Lloyd Sassman stationed on Grass Mountain; Siuslaw National Forest supervisor directing lookouts
Mr. and Mrs. Dave Cathcart Jr. caring for the lookout station
Mr. and Mrs. Devere Taylor stationed at Grass Mountain lookout; last staffing item found
Newly organized Polk-Benton District of the State Board of Forestry to occupy and maintain the station under an agreement
New tower erected for the lookout house (agency newsletter, quoted by Forest Lookouts); FFLOS and Forest Lookouts date the timber L-4 tower to 1951
October 12, 1962 windstorm; loss of the garage at the site
Lookout ground cabin constructed for $408.06 from the state restoration fund
FFLOS: removed in 1968. firelookout.com: destroyed 1968. Wikipedia: decommissioned and dismantled 1968. Forest Lookouts gives 1969.
Registered per FFLOS on November 8, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A Eugene newspaper in October 1934 reported the tower and house practically completed, so 1934 is recorded as the built event. FFLOS and Wikipedia say 1935; both dates are kept in the event notes.
Three sources give 1968 (FFLOS removed, firelookout.com destroyed, Wikipedia dismantled); Forest Lookouts gives 1969. Recorded as 1968 with the 1969 date noted.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1934 vs 1935), the 1950/1951 tower and its height (40 ft FFLOS vs 42 ft Forest Lookouts), and the removal year (1968 vs 1969) are unresolved source disagreements; the story reports them. Current access and ownership of the site are not described by any official source; the Summit Post report is user-written. Brief elevation 1100.9 m matches FFLOS 1,101 m, so no correction. Brief has no design or height, which are now filled from sources.
